rows.text: The Assembly's item of 20 July 2012 reports that 'KING Tupou VI has appointed Lord Fakafanua as the new Speaker of the Legislative Assembly', following the Assembly's nomination 'yesterday, Thursday 19th of July 2012', when of two nominations 17 members voted for Lord Fakafanua and eight for 'the number 2 Vava'u Noble representative', with Prime Minister Lord Tu'ivakano and Minister Fe'ao Vakata abstaining; Lord Fakafanua replaces the former Speaker Lord Lasike, whose post was revoked after his conviction.
rows.uncertainty: It reports the appointment as done by 20 July 2012 without dating it; the day is given by the Assembly's 23 July item (to_fakafanua_royal_appointment_20120719). The item names Lord Tu'ilakepa only as 'the former Speaker' in paragraph 3; his identity with 'the number 2 Vava'u Noble representative' of paragraph 4 is linked from MIC's release (to_fakafanua_assembly_election_20120719). The vote is the same event as that release's election.

rows.text: The same item says that 'At the same time, the Legislative Assembly is adjourned until further notice to inform His Majesty King Tupou VI on the outcome of the ballot', a procedure that, it says, 'the Legislative Act 2010 Act' [sic] requires before a new Speaker of Parliament is sworn in.
rows.uncertainty: The item does not record that the King was informed, and it does not date the adjournment ('At the same time'), so no structured date is stored. No Speaker's oath was found.

bounded_scope: Speaker observations for CLAUDE-C01-24 only (role to_speaker on the to_legislative_assembly observation). Royal appointment, the Assembly's election or recommendation of its Speaker, the oath, a resignation, a revocation, an acting or interim Speaker and a Deputy Speaker presiding stay separate rows; holder observations are decided in the packet, not by any row.
